segments.t: Barinov has lost money and wants more to bet. He phones Dmitry Nagiyev, the owner of Claude Monet, in the hope of an advance. Take it in once, and don't worry about the details.
Я тебе две зарплаты уже выдал.
Да я не за деньгами звоню!
Да, и у меня есть верная информация!
Мне нужен небольшой аванс до завтра.
Now the same thing, but slowly.

'Dmitry Vladimirovich, good morning to you!' Russians address respected people by first name and father's name: the patronymic is "son of Vladimir". The greeting is "kind morning", with Notice the part 'to you' added for extra politeness.

'Hey, Viktor, I am not giving you money!' The first word here is a casual "hi", spelled like In Russian, 'great' translates, but stressed on the first vowel. The phrase for not giving money means "of money not I'll give": In Russian, 'money' translates changes its ending after the negative word.
Я тебе две зарплаты уже выдал.

'I already paid you two paychecks.' Here, 'two' shows is the form for she-word words, because Here, 'paycheck' shows ends in a she-word vowel. The action word means "handed out", the word for paying wages. Nagiyev is counting, and the count is against Barinov.

'What did you want?' The way to express 'what' is the form of the question word that often goes with the action The way to express 'want', and it sounds casual. The action The way to express 'wanted' has the he-word past time frame ending. Nagiyev knows what the chef is after.
Да я не за деньгами звоню!

'Why, I am not calling for money!' The little 'yes' is used here here doesn't mean "yes". It works like "why" or "well". 'for money' is used here means "to fetch money": after the connecting word, 'money' is used here changes its ending.

'Really? Then why are you calling?' Here Listen to how 'yes' with a rising voice means "really?". Listen to how 'why' means "what for", as Barinov said to Tanya. The action Listen to how 'are calling' is the casual you form.

'Tonight is an important football match.' The speaker uses 'tonight' literally means "today in the evening". The speaker uses 'football' is turned into a describing word. Barinov names the thing on his mind.

'Is your beloved Spartak playing again?' They express 'beloved' by or "favourite" gives the word the mother used in the first scene. They express 'your' by gives the casual "your". The action word means "is playing".
Да, и у меня есть верная информация!
'Yes, and I have reliable insider info!' We hear 'there is' appears again: the phrase literally means "at me there is". We hear 'reliable' echoes the word as "faithful" in Senya's "faithful friend".
'Viktor, sports betting is dangerous.' When they say 'bets on sport' is multiple, so When they say 'dangerous' is multiple too. Nagiyev sounds like a wise uncle. It is good advice.
Мне нужен небольшой аванс до завтра.

'I need a small advance until tomorrow.' Notice the part 'advance' means an advance on wages. Notice the part 'until tomorrow' is literal. Notice the part 'I need' means "to me needed", with Notice the part 'needed' bare because Notice the part 'advance' is he-word.
'I know your advances, Viktor.' Nagiyev puts In Russian, 'advance' translates into the multiple. That is a joke, since it means there have been many. The action word means "I know".
'You will not get a single kopeck!' Here, 'not a kopeck' shows is the strong "not a single". Here, 'kopeck' shows changes its ending. The action word means "you will get". His refusal is complete.

'Dmitry, you will regret this!' Barinov drops the patronymic, and with it the politeness, and uses the casual "you". The way to express 'will regret this' means "will regret about this". He ends the call with a threat he cannot carry out. Now put it all together.
Я тебе две зарплаты уже выдал.
Да я не за деньгами звоню!
Да, и у меня есть верная информация!
Мне нужен небольшой аванс до завтра.
Nagiyev won't lend a kopeck, and Barinov hangs up in a temper. The chef will have to look for money elsewhere. Bye for now.
